parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime is protective and visitor-facing exposures are thin. Self-declaration recognition since 2015, SOGI-inclusive hate-crime law in force since end-2024, incitement penalties covering gender identity, and a large visible community with open Pride signal institutional acceptance. No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented border or facility restrictions, no documented targeting of trans visitors, and no trans-specific killing with a denominator gap resolved toward safety. Dated resident-facing negatives (single custodial case, proposed 2025 imprisonment amendment at first stage only, healthcare waits, care restricted for minors) are climate signals that temper but do not drive a visitor score. Rising reported discrimination and hate-crime volume are raw counts without denominators. This sits in the Low Risk band, below aspirational.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. No reported border questioning, marker mismatch refusal, or scanner outing for trans visitors; no X-marker domestic equivalent, but a visitor's home documents are not processed locally.
entry_documents.protection: Self-declaration recognition culture and equality-matrix 'gender change legal, no restrictions' indicate document-respecting institutions.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport governs; no domestic marker process touches a visitor.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: One dated custodial case (2022 conviction, 2024 acquittal) involving one individual, not a pattern; a late-2025 first-stage amendment would limit a certificate's effect for imprisonment — not passed.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate Offences Act 2024 covers gender identity; courts functioned for the individual concerned.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Custody placement rules for a foreign visitor are uncertain but no adverse practice documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Not documented. No facility-access bans, bathroom codes, or ward/custody placement rules for visitors.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Equality framework and hate-crime statute cover public services; gender identity protected grounds added 2022.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National protective framework operates uniformly; subnational variation is minimal (one dated local event cancellation).

care_services.exposure: Severe resident-facing gaps: 2.5–10 year waits, single understaffed provider, restrictive gatekeeping; care 'legal but restricted for minors' could affect a travelling minor's continuity of care — uncertain for visitors.
care_services.protection: Care is legal; private sector exists; no denial of emergency care documented.
care_services.interaction: A visitor needing refills may face the same bottleneck; a travelling minor may encounter the minors restriction.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented rise in anti-LGBT prejudice (2025 university study) and 15% rise in reported hate crimes (2025), though top motives were racism/xenophobia; one local drag-event cancellation amid abuse.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Toughest-in-region hate-crime statute (2024) plus incitement penalties; formal 2018 state apologies for past criminalisation signal institutional repudiation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police record hate crimes, implying functioning reporting channels.

minors_guardians.exposure: Gender-affirming care restricted for minors; 2019 ministerial report proposed extension to 16–17-year-olds, not enacted; a travelling minor needing care may hit restriction.
minors_guardians.interaction: Resident-facing care policy; no documented effect on entry or custody of minors travelling with trans guardians.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific killing documented, no denominator for trans violence, no visitor-targeted incidents; prejudice rising per 2025 study.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate Offences Act 2024 enables prosecution; anonymous LGBTQ+ reporting form and equality-legislation links available to anyone reporting.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting machinery operates; conviction practice not documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Open questions: effect of custody placement absent passage of the 2025 amendment; hate-speech 'backdown' report unverified; no data on visitor experiences of care or facilities.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Hate-crime reporting form, incitement statute, equality protections (SO only for employment/housing — resident gap, light weight).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist on paper and institutions function; enforcement records thin.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar protective statutory framework and oversight culture; this jurisdiction has stronger hate-crime law but documented rising prejudice and no documented visitor-facing remedy cases, placing it around or slightly below 0.85-A.

Clearer above 0.75-C: no documented border detention or secondary-screening pattern; instead self-declaration culture and broad community visibility; the custody question is a single first-stage amendment, not operative exposure.

Materially safer than 0.55-B: no documented routine screening friction or discretionary refusal-of-entry pattern; protections are in force with enforcement machinery, not merely appeal desks with stalled outcomes.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines strong, in-force protective law (self-declaration recognition, SOGI hate-crime statute, incitement penalties) with an open social sphere and no documented visitor-facing restriction on entry, facilities, or expression. The documented negatives — healthcare bottlenecks, minors' care restriction, rising prejudice, one dated custodial case, a stalled custody amendment — are predominantly resident-facing or prospective, weighing as climate signals under the rubric. Unknowns (custody placement, visitor care continuity) are open questions, not exposures. The result is a Low Risk jurisdiction: minor and plausible friction, no credible pathway to detention or severe harm on discovery, but not a zero-discrimination society.
